subject: chemistry_2
question_text: What are the monomer repeating units of nylon-6 and nylon-6,6?

verification.note: Unit 12 (Polymers), printed as VSAQ 15 on book p.97. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM, not the board scheme, until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. Source: the chemistry half of "FAST TRACK IPE for Sr. Students", printed chapter 9 (POLYMERS), book pp.95-98 (PDF pp.34-37), which is unit 12 in this bank. The chapter is VSAQ-only: it prints 24 Very Short Answer Questions and has no Short Answer and no Long Answer section at all, and no PROBLEMS. Neither the two-book union check nor a board back-test was possible for Chemistry-II: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is physics-only and first-year, and no second-year chemistry paper is in the corpus. BOOK SPELLING AND GAP: the printed answer is "In Nylon-6, monomer is caprolactum. In Nylon-6, 6, monomers are hexamethylene diamine and adipic acid." The chemistry is correct and is kept; caprolactum is a misspelling of caprolactam and is corrected. The question asks for the repeating UNITS and the printed answer gives only monomer names, no units at all; both repeating units are written here.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Nylon-6
lines: Nylon-6 is made from one monomer,
One monomer means nylon-6 is a
steps.why: Caprolactam is a ring, so no water is released when it opens: the ring breaks at its amide bond and the two ends join the neighbours. That is why nylon-6 needs only one starting material while nylon-6,6 needs two.
common_mistakes: Writing the monomer of nylon-6 as hexamethylene diamine. That is a monomer of nylon-6,6.
Spelling it caprolactum. It is caprolactam, because it is a lactam, a cyclic amide.
steps.memory_tip: Nylon-6 has one 6 in its name, so one monomer with six carbons.
steps.margin_note: Naming caprolactam is the mark. The repeating unit is one extra line and makes it safe.

steps.label: Nylon-6,6
lines: Nylon-6,6 is made from two monomers:
Two monomers mean nylon-6,6 is a
copolymer, and one water molecule is
steps.why: Both monomers have six carbons, and the two sixes in the name record that. Adipic acid shows only four –CH₂– groups because two of its six carbons are the –COOH carbons, and that count is the one students most often get wrong.
common_mistakes: Writing adipic acid as HOOC–(CH₂)₆–COOH. It is HOOC–(CH₂)₄–COOH; the two –COOH carbons make the total six.
Giving caprolactam as a monomer of nylon-6,6. Caprolactam belongs to nylon-6.
steps.memory_tip: Nylon-6,6 has two sixes in its name, so two monomers of six carbons each.
steps.margin_note: Both monomer names are the mark. Add the repeating unit, because this question asks for units.

insider_note: The number of sixes in the name is the number of monomers. Nylon-6 has one and nylon-6,6 has two.
